nvd.description:
Why is Microsoft republishing a CVE from 2013?
We are republishing CVE-2013-3900 in the Security Update Guide to update the Security Updates table and to inform customers that the EnableCertPaddingCheck is available in all currently supported versions of Windows 10 and Windows 11. While the format is different from the original CVE published in 2013, except for clarifications about how to configure the EnableCertPaddingCheck registry value, the information herein remains unchanged from the original text published on December 10, 2013,
Microsoft does not plan to enforce the stricter verification behavior as a default functionality on supported releases of Microsoft Windows. This behavior remains available as an opt-in feature via reg key setting, and is available on supported editions of Windows released since December 10, 2013. This includes all currently supported versions of Windows 10 and Windows 11. The supporting code for this reg key was incorporated at the time of release for Windows 10 and Windows 11, so no security update is required; however, the reg key must be set. See the Security Updates table for the list of affected software.
Vulnerability Description
A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the way that the WinVerifyTrust function handles Windows Authenticode signature verification for portable executable (PE) files. An anonymous attacker could exploit the vulnerability by modifying an existing signed executable file to leverage unverified portions of the file in such a way as to add malicious code to the file without invalidating the signature. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could take complete control of an affected system. An attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights.
If a user is logged on with administrative user rights, an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could take complete control of an affected system. An attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. Users whose accounts are configured to have fewer user rights on the system could be less impacted than users who operate with administrative user rights.

nvd.description:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists in Windows when the Windows kernel-mode driver fails to properly handle objects in memory. An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could run arbitrary code in kernel mode. An attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights.
To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system. An attacker could then run a specially crafted application that could exploit the vulnerability and take control of an affected system.
The update addresses this vulnerability by correcting how the Windows kernel-mode driver handles objects in memory.

nvd.description: Multiple ZyXEL network-attached storage (NAS) devices running firmware version 5.21 contain a pre-authentication command injection vulnerability, which may allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on a vulnerable device. ZyXEL NAS devices achieve authentication by using the weblogin.cgi CGI executable. This program fails to properly sanitize the username parameter that is passed to it. If the username parameter contains certain characters, it can allow command injection with the privileges of the web server that runs on the ZyXEL device. Although the web server does not run as the root user, ZyXEL devices include a setuid utility that can be leveraged to run any command with root privileges. As such, it should be assumed that exploitation of this vulnerability can lead to remote code execution with root privileges. By sending a specially-crafted HTTP POST or GET request to a vulnerable ZyXEL device, a remote, unauthenticated attacker may be able to execute arbitrary code on the device. This may happen by directly connecting to a device if it is directly exposed to an attacker. However, there are ways to trigger such crafted requests even if an attacker does not have direct connectivity to a vulnerable devices. For example, simply visiting a website can result in the compromise of any ZyXEL device that is reachable from the client system. Affected products include: NAS326 before firmware V5.21(AAZF.7)C0 NAS520 before firmware V5.21(AASZ.3)C0 NAS540 before firmware V5.21(AATB.4)C0 NAS542 before firmware V5.21(ABAG.4)C0 ZyXEL has made firmware updates available for NAS326, NAS520, NAS540, and NAS542 devices. Affected models that are end-of-support: NSA210, NSA220, NSA220+, NSA221, NSA310, NSA310S, NSA320, NSA320S, NSA325 and NSA325v2

If the attacker has admin panel access to an account with permission to access the username and email of API users with a lower privileged role (e.g., Editor or Author), then this can be exploited to discover sensitive information for all API users but not other admin accounts.

cisa_kev.title: Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software SNMP Denial of Service and Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
cisa_kev.description: Cisco IOS and IOS XE contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem that could allow for denial of service or remote code execution. A successful exploit could allow a low-privileged attacker to cause the affected system to reload, resulting in a DoS condition, or allow a high-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary code as the root user and obtain full control of the affected system.

nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) subsystem of Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software could allow the following:
  An authenticated, remote attacker with low privileges could cause a denial of service (DoS) condition on an affected device that is running Cisco IOS Software or Cisco IOS XE Software. To cause the DoS, the attacker must have the SNMPv2c or earlier read-only community string or valid SNMPv3 user credentials.  An authenticated, remote attacker with high privileges could execute code as the root user on an affected device that is running Cisco IOS XE Software. To execute code as the root user, the attacker must have the SNMPv1 or v2c read-only community string or valid SNMPv3 user credentials and administrative or privilege 15 credentials on the affected device.   An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted SNMP packet to an affected device over IPv4 or IPv6 networks. 
 This vulnerability is due to a stack overflow condition in the SNMP subsystem of the affected software. A successful exploit could allow a low-privileged attacker to cause the affected system to reload, resulting in a DoS condition, or allow a high-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary code as the root user and obtain full control of the affected system.
 Note: This vulnerability affects all versions of SNMP.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

posix-cpu-timers: fix race between handle_posix_cpu_timers() and posix_cpu_timer_del()

If an exiting non-autoreaping task has already passed exit_notify() and
calls handle_posix_cpu_timers() from IRQ, it can be reaped by its parent
or debugger right after unlock_task_sighand().

If a concurrent posix_cpu_timer_del() runs at that moment, it won't be
able to detect timer->it.cpu.firing != 0: cpu_timer_task_rcu() and/or
lock_task_sighand() will fail.

Add the tsk->exit_state check into run_posix_cpu_timers() to fix this.

This fix is not needed if CONFIG_POSIX_CPU_TIMERS_TASK_WORK=y, because
exit_task_work() is called before exit_notify(). But the check still
makes sense, task_work_add(&tsk->posix_cputimers_work.work) will fail
anyway in this case.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tls: fix handling of zero-length records on the rx_list

Each recvmsg() call must process either
 - only contiguous DATA records (any number of them)
 - one non-DATA record

If the next record has different type than what has already been
processed we break out of the main processing loop. If the record
has already been decrypted (which may be the case for TLS 1.3 where
we don't know type until decryption) we queue the pending record
to the rx_list. Next recvmsg() will pick it up from there.

Queuing the skb to rx_list after zero-copy decrypt is not possible,
since in that case we decrypted directly to the user space buffer,
and we don't have an skb to queue (darg.skb points to the ciphertext
skb for access to metadata like length).

Only data records are allowed zero-copy, and we break the processing
loop after each non-data record. So we should never zero-copy and
then find out that the record type has changed. The corner case
we missed is when the initial record comes from rx_list, and it's
zero length.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

crypto: af_alg - Disallow concurrent writes in af_alg_sendmsg

Issuing two writes to the same af_alg socket is bogus as the
data will be interleaved in an unpredictable fashion.  Furthermore,
concurrent writes may create inconsistencies in the internal
socket state.

Disallow this by adding a new ctx->write field that indiciates
exclusive ownership for writing.

nvd.description: Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control system with an unusually rich command set that provides both high-level operations and full access to internals. When reading a config value, Git strips any trailing carriage return and line feed (CRLF). When writing a config entry, values with a trailing CR are not quoted, causing the CR to be lost when the config is later read. When initializing a submodule, if the submodule path contains a trailing CR, the altered path is read resulting in the submodule being checked out to an incorrect location. If a symlink exists that points the altered path to the submodule hooks directory, and the submodule contains an executable post-checkout hook, the script may be unintentionally executed after checkout. This vulnerability is fixed in v2.43.7, v2.44.4, v2.45.4, v2.46.4, v2.47.3, v2.48.2, v2.49.1, and v2.50.1.

nvd.description: GeoServer is an open source server that allows users to share and edit geospatial data. nvd.description: Ray is an AI compute engine. Prior to version 2.52.0, developers working with Ray as a development tool can be exploited via a critical RCE vulnerability exploitable via Firefox and Safari. This vulnerability is due to an insufficient guard against browser-based attacks, as the current defense uses the User-Agent header starting with the string "Mozilla" as a defense mechanism. This defense is insufficient as the fetch specification allows the User-Agent header to be modified. Combined with a DNS rebinding attack against the browser, and this vulnerability is exploitable against a developer running Ray who inadvertently visits a malicious website, or is served a malicious advertisement (malvertising). This issue has been patched in version 2.52.0.

nvd.description: n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Versions starting with 0.211.0 and prior to 1.120.4, 1.121.1, and 1.122.0 contain a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in their workflow expression evaluation system. Under certain conditions, expressions supplied by authenticated users during workflow configuration may be evaluated in an execution context that is not sufficiently isolated from the underlying runtime. An authenticated attacker could abuse this behavior to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the n8n process. Successful exploitation may lead to full compromise of the affected instance, including unauthorized access to sensitive data, modification of workflows, and execution of system-level operations. This issue has been fixed in versions 1.120.4, 1.121.1, and 1.122.0. Users are strongly advised to upgrade to a patched version, which introduces additional safeguards to restrict expression evaluation. If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations: Limit workflow creation and editing permissions to fully trusted users only; and/or deploy n8n in a hardened environment with restricted operating system privileges and network access to reduce the impact of potential exploitation. These workarounds do not fully eliminate the risk and should only be used as short-term measures.

context: Zammad GmbH Zammad contains an improper privilege management vulnerability that can allow the local zammad user to escalate privileges to root. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-102489.

nvd.description: Zammad packages built with packager.io (DEB and RPM) could have allowed a local attacker who already had file system write privileges as the unprivileged zammad service account to escalate to full root privileges on the host. Service processes began running as root and executed files that were owned and writable by the zammad account before dropping their identity to that account. An attacker holding that foothold could have escalated within seconds, because the affected services were restarted automatically whenever they stopped; no administrator interaction was required. Only installations from the DEB and RPM packages were affected — installations from source or the official container images were not. All released packaged versions were affected.

nvd.description: GPUStack is an open-source GPU cluster manager for AI model serving and GPU instance provisioning. Prior to 2.2.0, get_current_user in gpustack/api/auth.py treated a loopback request source as the built-in administrator when force_auth_localhost was false, which was the default. A remote request could appear to originate from 127.0.0.1 because client_ip_getter accepted a same-host reverse proxy peer or a client-supplied X-GPUStack-Real-IP loopback value. The bypass allowed unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml. Exploitation was observed in the wild against a 2.1.1 deployment. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.0.

nvd.description: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.3, sofia_presence_handle_sip_i_message() split the To user of an inbound SIP MESSAGE on a plus sign and treated the left side as a chat protocol selector. Selecting the api chat proto reached switch_api_execute(), allowing a peer whose MESSAGE was accepted to run FreeSWITCH API commands, including operating-system command sinks, with the daemon's privileges. Inbound chat is enabled on the stock internal and external profiles, and any authenticated profile account is sufficient; stock directory users without password material can also remove that barrier in affected configurations. The flaw permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution, and exploitation has been observed in the wild. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.3.

nvd.description:
Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

A vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager (Unified CM) and Cisco Unified Communications Manager Session Management Edition (Unified CM SME) could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to conduct server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks through an affected device.

This vulnerability is due to improper input validation for specific HTTP requests. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.
Note: Cisco has assigned this security advisory a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of Critical rather than High as the score indicates. The reason is that exploitation of this vulnerability could result in an attacker elevating privileges to root.
Note: To exploit this vulnerability, the WebDialer service must be enabled. WebDialer is disabled by default.

nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the Remote Access SSL VPN service for Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to the Remote Access SSL VPN service on an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition.

nvd.description: This is a vulnerability in Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center. Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye. This Arbitrary File Access vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. nvd.description:
Improper Input Validation, Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ Broker, Apache ActiveMQ.

Apache ActiveMQ Classic exposes the Jolokia JMX-HTTP bridge at /api/jolokia/ on the web console. The default Jolokia access policy permits exec operations on all ActiveMQ MBeans (org.apache.activemq:*), including
BrokerService.addNetworkConnector(String) and BrokerService.addConnector(String).

An authenticated attacker can invoke these operations with a crafted discovery URI that triggers the VM transport's brokerConfig parameter to load a remote Spring XML application context using ResourceXmlApplicationContext.
Because Spring's ResourceXmlApplicationContext instantiates all singleton beans before the BrokerService validates the configuration, arbitrary code execution occurs on the broker's JVM through bean factory methods such as Runtime.exec().



This issue affects Apache ActiveMQ Broker: before 5.19.4, from 6.0.0 before 6.2.3; Apache ActiveMQ All: before 5.19.4, from 6.0.0 before 6.2.3; Apache ActiveMQ: before 5.19.4, from 6.0.0 before 6.2.3.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 5.19.4 or 6.2.3, which fixes the issue

nvd.description: LiteLLM is a proxy server (AI Gateway) to call LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format. From version 1.81.16 to before version 1.83.7, a database query used during proxy API key checks mixed the caller-supplied key value into the query text instead of passing it as a separate parameter. An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted Authorization header to any LLM API route (for example POST /chat/completions) and reach this query through the proxy's error-handling path. An attacker could read data from the proxy's database and may be able to modify it, leading to unauthorised access to the proxy and the credentials it manages. This issue has been patched in version 1.83.7.

nvd.description: LiteLLM is a proxy server (AI Gateway) to call LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format. From version 1.74.2 to before version 1.83.7, two endpoints used to preview an MCP server before saving it — POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list — accepted a full server configuration in the request body, including the command, args, and env fields used by the stdio transport. When called with a stdio configuration, the endpoints attempted to connect, which spawned the supplied command as a subprocess on the proxy host with the privileges of the proxy process. The endpoints were gated only by a valid proxy API key, with no role check. Any authenticated user — including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys — could therefore run arbitrary commands on the host. This issue has been patched in version 1.83.7.

nvd.description: On 2026-05-11, between approximately 19:20 and 19:26 UTC, 84 malicious versions across 42 @tanstack/* packages were published to the npm registry. The publishes were authenticated via the legitimate GitHub Actions OIDC trusted-publisher binding for TanStack/router, but the publish workflow itself was not modified. The attacker chained three known vulnerability classes — a pull_request_target "Pwn Request" misconfiguration, GitHub Actions cache poisoning across the fork↔base trust boundary, and runtime memory extraction of the OIDC token from the Actions runner process — to publish credential-stealing malware under a trusted identity. Each affected package received exactly two malicious versions, published a few minutes apart.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing

skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @from to @to.  If @from
has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same
externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker
is currently lost.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  In
particular, ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding
whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data().  If TCP
receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can
see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache
backed frags.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when skb_try_coalesce() transfers paged
frags.  The tailroom copy path does not need the marker because it copies
bytes into @to's linear data rather than transferring frag descriptors.

nvd.description: Starlette is a lightweight ASGI framework/toolkit. Prior to version 1.0.1, the HTTP `Host` request header was not validated before being used to reconstruct `request.url`. Because the routing algorithm relies on the raw HTTP path while `request.url` is rebuilt from the `Host` header, a malformed header could make `request.url.path` differ from the path that was actually requested. Middleware and endpoints that apply security restrictions based on `request.url` (rather than the raw `scope` path) could therefore be bypassed. Users should upgrade to a version greater than or equal to version 1.0.1, which validates the `Host` header against the grammar of RFC 9112 §3.2 / RFC 3986 §3.2.2 when constructing `request.url` and falls back to `scope["server"]` for malformed values.

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: bridge: make ebt_snat ARP rewrite writable

The ebtables SNAT target keeps the Ethernet source address rewrite
behind skb_ensure_writable(skb, 0).  This is intentional: at the bridge
ebtables hooks the Ethernet header is addressed through
skb_mac_header()/eth_hdr(), while skb->data points at the Ethernet
payload.  Asking skb_ensure_writable() for ETH_HLEN bytes would check
the payload, not the Ethernet header, and would reintroduce the small
packet regression fixed by commit 63137bc5882a.

However, the optional ARP sender hardware address rewrite is different.
It writes through skb_store_bits() at an offset relative to skb->data:

        skb_store_bits(skb, sizeof(struct arphdr), info->mac, ETH_ALEN)

skb_header_pointer() only safely reads the ARP header; it does not make
the later sender hardware address range writable.  If that range is
still held in a nonlinear skb fragment backed by a splice-imported file
page, skb_store_bits() maps the frag page and copies the new MAC address
directly into it.

Ensure the ARP SHA range is writable before reading the ARP header and
before calling skb_store_bits().

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: account for fraggap on the paged allocation path

In __ip6_append_data(), when the paged-allocation branch is taken
(MSG_MORE / NETIF_F_SG / large fraglen), alloclen and pagedlen are
computed as

	alloclen = fragheaderlen + transhdrlen;
	pagedlen = datalen - transhdrlen;

datalen already includes fraggap (datalen = length + fraggap). When
fraggap is non-zero, this is not the first skb and transhdrlen is zero.
The fraggap bytes carried over from the previous skb are copied just past
the fragment headers in the new skb's linear area. The linear area is
therefore undersized by fraggap bytes while pagedlen is overstated by the
same amount, and the copy writes past skb->end into the trailing
skb_shared_info.

An unprivileged user can trigger this via a UDPv6 socket using
MSG_MORE together with MSG_SPLICE_PAGES.

The bad accounting was introduced by commit 773ba4fe9104 ("ipv6:
avoid partial copy for zc"). Before commit ce650a166335 ("udp6: Fix
__ip6_append_data()'s handling of MSG_SPLICE_PAGES"), the negative
copy value caused -EINVAL to be returned. That later commit allowed
MSG_SPLICE_PAGES to proceed in this case, making the corruption
triggerable.

The non-paged branch sets alloclen to fraglen, which already accounts
for fraggap because datalen does. Bring the paged branch in line by
adding fraggap to alloclen and subtracting it from pagedlen.

After this adjustment, copy no longer collapses to -fraggap on the
paged path, so remove the stale comment describing that old arithmetic.
Since a negative copy is no longer expected for a valid MSG_SPLICE_PAGES
case, remove the MSG_SPLICE_PAGES exception from the negative copy check.

nvd.description: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. Starting in 3.3.0 and prior to 3.15.0, the POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test endpoint (accessible without credentials when server authentication is not enabled) calls _validate_webhook_url() in mlflow/utils/validation.py only for the original URL while mlflow/webhooks/delivery.py follows redirects and re-resolves the hostname without pinning the validated address, allowing attackers to reach internal or cloud metadata services and receive response_status and response_body. The unauthenticated attack scenario described here applies to deployments without authentication. With MLflow’s built-in basic authentication enabled, requests to this endpoint require valid credentials; this issue does not itself bypass authentication. This issue is fixed in version 3.15.0.

This issue has been reported as being exploited in the wild.

An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands. nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system.

This vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system.

nvd.description:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation. When a SOAP <Fault> carries a <detail><exceptionName> element, Axis loads the named class and, if a String <data> element is also present, instantiates it through its String constructor before checking that it is an AxisFault. Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's classpath this leads to remote code execution. The fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it. This affects all Apache Axis 1.x versions through 1.4.



As Axis 1 has been EOL we recommend you migrate to a different SOAP engine, such as Apache Axis 2/Java. The Apache Axis project does not expect to create an Axis 1.x release fixing this problem.

context: Microsoft Windows CryptoAPI (Crypt32.dll) contains a spoofing vulnerability in the way it validates Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) certificates. The vulnerability is also known under the moniker of CurveBall.

context: Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that exists in the Classic Web Client due to insufficient sanitization of HTML content in ICS files. When a user views an e-mail message containing a malicious ICS entry, its embedded JavaScript executes via an ontoggle event inside a tag. This allows an attacker to run arbitrary JavaScript within the victim's session, potentially leading to unauthorized actions such as setting e-mail filters to redirect messages to an attacker-controlled address. As a result, an attacker can perform unauthorized actions on the victim's account, including e-mail redirection and data exfiltration.

context:
The system call verification handlers for smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() in drivers/smbus/smbus_handlers.c (z_vrfy_smbus_block_read() and z_vrfy_smbus_block_pcall()) validated the device object, the count pointers and (for process call) the send buffer, but never validated the receive buffer (buf / rcv_buf). The call then proceeds into the driver implementation, which runs in supervisor mode and writes the bytes received from the SMBus peripheral through that pointer.

A user-mode thread on a system built with CONFIG_USERSPACE that has been granted access to an SMBus device object can pass an arbitrary address, including kernel data or another thread's memory, as the receive buffer. The driver then writes up to SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes of peripheral-supplied data there (the STM32 driver writes as many bytes as the peripheral's length byte announces, up to 255). The address is fully attacker-chosen; the written content comes from the bus and is typically influenceable by the caller through the choice of peripheral and command, or by first writing data to a device that echoes it back.

This breaks the user/kernel isolation boundary: it gives an unprivileged thread a kernel-memory write primitive usable for privilege escalation, or at minimum to corrupt kernel state or crash the system. The fix adds K_SYSCALL_MEMORY_WRITE() checks of the receive buffer for the documented worst case, SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX. Systems without CONFIG_USERSPACE are not affected.

nvd.description:
The system call verification handlers for smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() in drivers/smbus/smbus_handlers.c (z_vrfy_smbus_block_read() and z_vrfy_smbus_block_pcall()) validated the device object, the count pointers and (for process call) the send buffer, but never validated the receive buffer (buf / rcv_buf). The call then proceeds into the driver implementation, which runs in supervisor mode and writes the bytes received from the SMBus peripheral through that pointer.

A user-mode thread on a system built with CONFIG_USERSPACE that has been granted access to an SMBus device object can pass an arbitrary address, including kernel data or another thread's memory, as the receive buffer. The driver then writes up to SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes of peripheral-supplied data there (the STM32 driver writes as many bytes as the peripheral's length byte announces, up to 255). The address is fully attacker-chosen; the written content comes from the bus and is typically influenceable by the caller through the choice of peripheral and command, or by first writing data to a device that echoes it back.

This breaks the user/kernel isolation boundary: it gives an unprivileged thread a kernel-memory write primitive usable for privilege escalation, or at minimum to corrupt kernel state or crash the system. The fix adds K_SYSCALL_MEMORY_WRITE() checks of the receive buffer for the documented worst case, SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX. Systems without CONFIG_USERSPACE are not affected.

Several Bluetooth LE Audio services in subsys/bluetooth/audio register global connection and authentication callbacks but assume every connection is LE. When CONFIG_BT_CLASSIC is enabled, the host also invokes these callbacks for BR/EDR connections. For such connections bt_conn_get_dst() returns NULL, and bt_conn_get_info() leaves info.le.dst unset (zero or uninitialized stack data). The CSIP Set Member (csip_disconnected(), handle_csip_disconnect(), handle_csip_auth_complete()), PACS (pacs_auth_pairing_complete(), pacs_security_changed()) and HAS (security_changed(), client_alloc(), client_free()) callbacks then compare or copy a Bluetooth address through that NULL or uninitialized pointer.

A remote device within Bluetooth range can trigger this against a dual-mode device that exposes LE Audio server roles and accepts BR/EDR connections. Opening and closing a BR/EDR ACL link, with no pairing, reaches the CSIP Set Member disconnect path. Completing SSP pairing (for example Just Works) or encryption reaches the PACS and HAS paths.

The impact is denial of service. With CONFIG_ASSERT enabled, the device halts on an assertion (bt_keys_find_addr(), context_alloc()). On platforms that trap NULL or wild reads, it crashes. Otherwise, internal PACS/CSIP/HAS client state is corrupted with bogus addresses. The defects are reads only, and the attacker does not control the address that is dereferenced. The fix adds bt_conn_is_type(conn, BT_CONN_TYPE_LE) checks at the top of the affected callbacks.

context:
The Intel SEDI I2C controller driver (drivers/i2c/i2c_sedi.c, used on Intel ISH platforms) waits for each asynchronous transfer with k_sem_take() on a per-controller completion semaphore and a 1 s timeout. When the wait times out, i2c_sedi_api_full_io() aborts the transfer via SEDI_I2C_ABORT_TRANSFER, but if the controller's completion interrupt fires between the timeout expiring and the abort masking interrupts, the callback k_sem_give()s the semaphore and the token is never discarded.

The next transfer on that bus then takes the stale token immediately and returns success (the stale context->err is usually 0) while the controller is still executing it. The HAL interrupt handler (or DMA) keeps copying received bytes into the caller's msgs[i].buf. Since I2C callers typically pass stack buffers, this writes into a stack frame that has already been returned from, and the caller also consumes incomplete data. The desynchronization can persist across later transfers.

Triggering the race requires a transfer to complete just after the 1 s timeout. A device on the I2C bus that controls clock stretching (for example a malicious or tampered peripheral) can steer this timing, and it also supplies the bytes that get written. Exploitation therefore needs physical access to the bus and is timing-dependent. The impact is corruption of kernel or thread stack memory with data the peripheral controls, which can lead to a crash or potentially to code execution. The fix calls k_sem_reset() and clears context->err after the abort, while the transfer mutex is still held.

The mount-time recovery scan of the Zephyr Memory Storage (ZMS) key-value store, zms_recover_last_ate() in subsys/kvss/zms/zms.c (subsys/fs/zms/zms.c in older releases), computes the end of the sector's data area incorrectly. Every valid allocation table entry (ATE) reset the data-end bound to the start of the sector, including entries whose value is stored inline (8 bytes or less) and delete entries. When the newest ATE in the active sector is one of these, the scan continues past the ATE area into the payload area and reads stored value bytes as struct zms_ate records.

Any payload slot that passes the ATE check (a CRC8 plus the one-byte sector cycle count) is adopted as the newest entry. zms_init() then sets fs->ate_wra and fs->data_wra from it. The pointers are only this weak check away from data an application may have stored on behalf of a remote party: a BLE-writable device name, provisioned credentials, or configuration received over the network. An attacker who can get about 16 bytes of chosen content persisted in a ZMS value can plant a forged ATE. The forged entry takes effect after the next mount, provided the newest entry in that sector is small or a delete. Random data can also match by chance, which is how the issue was found.

A forged or accidentally matched ATE overrides the stored entry for any chosen id. Its inline data or its offset/len pointer controls what later reads of that key return. The misplaced write pointers also make later writes place ATEs and payloads over other entries' existing data, silently corrupting persistent configuration such as settings values stored in ZMS. The effects are limited to the active flash sector and to what ZMS returns to its callers. No RAM out-of-bounds access was identified.

The Intel SoC FPGA Agilex5 SoC's static MMU region table in soc/intel/intel_socfpga/agilex5/mmu_regions.c mapped the System Manager peripheral (sysmgr) with MT_P_RW_U_RW. That sets the EL0 access-permission bit in the page-table descriptor, so user mode can read and write the block. The other peripheral windows in the same table, and the same block on the sibling Agilex SoC, are correctly mapped MT_P_RW_U_NA.

On arm64, memory-domain page tables are cloned from the kernel page tables (arch_mem_domain_init()). When CONFIG_USERSPACE is enabled, every user mode thread therefore gets direct load/store access to the System Manager registers, with no partition grant or system call. Any untrusted code running as a user thread can exploit this.

The System Manager controls system-wide state that only the kernel should own: NoC/FPGA-bridge idle requests, SDMMC and EMAC interface configuration, FPGA interface enables and boot scratch registers. A user thread can stall the interconnect or reconfigure peripherals out from under kernel drivers, causing denial of service and integrity loss for the platform, and can read that configuration. This breaks the userspace isolation boundary. Builds without CONFIG_USERSPACE (the default) are not affected. The fix maps the region MT_P_RW_U_NA.

context:
The Zephyr TFTP client in subsys/net/lib/tftp/tftp_client.c does not check where the reply to its request comes from. After sending a read or write request to the configured server, send_request() accepts the first UDP datagram that arrives on the client's socket from any address and port. It then calls zsock_connect() to that sender, so the sender becomes the peer for the rest of the transfer. RFC 1350 requires a client to discard datagrams whose source does not match the transfer ID it expects.

A host that can send a UDP datagram to the client's ephemeral port before the real server replies can take over the transfer. It can reply from its own address and does not need to spoof the server. A host on the same network segment that sees the request can do this easily. An off-path attacker must guess the randomized ephemeral port and win the race, which is easier when the server is slow or unreachable. No authentication or user interaction is needed beyond the device starting a transfer through tftp_get() or tftp_put(), for example from an application or the net tftp shell command.

For tftp_get(), the attacker chooses the entire content handed to the application's data callback. For tftp_put(), the whole upload buffer is sent to the attacker. There is no memory corruption. TFTP itself has no authentication, and after the fix an attacker who can spoof the server's IP address can still interfere with a transfer. The fix checks the server's address on the first reply and the full address and port on every later datagram, and drops mismatches without using up the transfer's retries.

context:
usbh_req_setup() in subsys/usb/host/usbh_ch9.c returns -ETIMEDOUT as soon as a control request times out, even though the transfer is still in flight. usbh_xfer_dequeue() only requests cancellation, and the host controller driver keeps the transfer and its data buffer until it returns it through the completion callback. Callers such as usbh_req_desc_dev() and usbh_req_desc_cfg() free the buffer (net_buf_unref()) right after usbh_req_setup() returns. Separately, a single global semaphore (ch9_req_sync) with no mutual exclusion lets a late or foreign completion wake the wrong waiter. That waiter then returns early and its caller frees a buffer the controller is still filling.

A malicious USB device attached to a Zephyr USB host port can trigger this during enumeration. It NAKs a GET_DESCRIPTOR request until the 5-second timeout expires, then answers with data around the cancellation, or delays its answer to the next request after leaving a stale semaphore signal. The controller driver (for example the MAX3421E max3421e_hrslt_success() path) then writes device-controlled bytes into the freed net_buf and updates its length.

The result is a use-after-free write into the USB host buffer pool with attacker-chosen contents, which can corrupt buffers that have been reallocated to other transfers, plus a leak of transfer objects. Crashes or memory corruption follow. The fix serializes usbh_req_setup() with a mutex, resets the semaphore before each request, and waits for the driver to return a cancelled transfer before freeing it. Only builds with the experimental CONFIG_USB_HOST_STACK are affected.

The STM32 SMBus driver (drivers/smbus/smbus_stm32.c) implements smbus_block_read() and smbus_block_pcall() by issuing a single i2c_transfer() in which the byte-count byte returned by the peripheral is read directly into the len field of the following i2c_msg. That message then receives data straight into the caller-supplied buffer. Nothing bounds the count, so smbus_stm32_block_read() and smbus_stm32_block_pcall() read up to 255 bytes into a buffer that the SMBus API documents (and the syscall verifiers validate) as holding at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX (32) bytes.

The count is chosen by the addressed SMBus peripheral. A malicious, counterfeit or faulty device on the bus (for example a removable smart battery, PMBus supply or plug-in module), or anyone able to drive the bus lines, can report a block count above 32 and cause the driver to write up to 223 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer. Callers typically pass a 32-byte stack buffer, as the in-tree smbus block_read shell command does, so the overflow lands on the caller's stack before any caller-side count check can run.

The result is attacker-controlled stack or memory corruption in the context of the calling thread, which can crash the system or potentially be leveraged for code execution. When the call arrives through the smbus_block_read/smbus_block_pcall system calls, the out-of-bounds write happens in supervisor mode beyond the 32-byte region validated for the user thread. The fix receives the block into a driver-local 255-byte buffer and copies it out only when the count is at most SMBUS_BLOCK_BYTES_MAX, returning -ENODATA otherwise.

The OpenThread PSA crypto platform backend in modules/openthread/platform/crypto_psa.c only supported PSA key references. otPlatCryptoAesSetKey() copied aKey->mKeyRef into the AES context unconditionally. On an OpenThread Radio Co-Processor (RCP) build, CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA does not select CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_PLATFORM_KEY_REF, so OpenThread passes the MAC key as literal bytes and mKeyRef is uninitialized. psa_cipher_encrypt() in otPlatCryptoAesEncrypt() then fails without writing its output, and the error is only caught by an OpenThread assertion that is compiled to a no-op when CONFIG_ASSERT is disabled.

When the RCP handles transmit security in software, AES-CCM* is never keyed. That is the case with Thread 1.2 or later, where CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_MAC_SOFTWARE_TX_SECURITY_ENABLE defaults to y, on a radio driver without IEEE802154_HW_TX_SEC. Every MAC key-id-mode-1 frame goes out with its payload XORed against a single 16-byte pad of stale stack data, reused for every block, and with an unkeyed MIC. CONFIG_OPENTHREAD_CRYPTO_PSA is enabled by default since v4.4.0.

A passive attacker within 802.15.4 radio range can recover the pad from predictable plaintext (for example 6LoWPAN headers) and read the payload of the frames the device transmits. The practical impact is limited. The configuration is not the default (the default Thread version is 1.1), and the same defect makes peers reject every secured data frame, so an affected device cannot exchange data on the network. Received traffic and key distribution are not affected. With CONFIG_ASSERT enabled, the RCP halts on the first secured transmission instead.

ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c dropped the caller's reference on an IPv4 packet whenever net_arp_prepare() returned NET_ARP_PKT_REPLACED. That return value is also used when ARP could not queue the packet because every ARP cache entry is already pending. In that case ARP holds no reference of its own, so the original packet was freed before the replacing ARP request was transmitted.

If transmitting the ARP request then failed (a driver send error or an ethernet_fill_header() failure), the error path called net_pkt_ref() on the freed packet. net_if_tx() then called net_pkt_unref() on it again. If the freed net_pkt slab slot was reallocated in between, the stray unref releases a reference owned by an unrelated packet, which is freed while still in use.

An attacker on the local link can drive the ARP cache into the all-pending state. CONFIG_NET_ARP_TABLE_SIZE defaults to 2, so it is enough to elicit replies to a few spoofed, non-responding on-subnet addresses. Reaching the memory corruption also needs a transmit failure the attacker does not directly control and a narrow slab-reuse race. The practical impact is corruption or a crash of the network stack (denial of service).

context: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 2.1.0 until 4.5.2, get_eacontent in libatalk/vfs/ea_ad.c subtracts MAX_REPLY_EXTRA_BYTES from a client-controlled FPGetExtAttr MaxReplySize without rejecting values from 1 through 5, and a signed-to-unsigned comparison can then select an untrusted AppleDouble ea_size. An authenticated client on a volume configured with ea = ad can use a pre-existing malformed AppleDouble sidecar to make read copy attacker-controlled bytes beyond dsi->data + 6 into the surrounding struct DSI, including protocol callback pointers. The malformed sidecar must already exist or be created through a separate local, co-export, management, restore, or vulnerability-assisted write path, and practical code execution depends on the target architecture, structure layout, and address uncertainty; runtime command execution was demonstrated on one x86-64 build. Volumes using ea = sys, ea = none, or ea = auto when it resolves to native system xattrs do not reach this path. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

context: The WP Compress – Instant Performance & Speed Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 7.26.00 via the 'css' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Exploiting the file read requires a preparatory unauthenticated request that plants a boundary directory by injecting a path traversal sequence into a cookie listed in WPC_CACHE_COOKIES (such as pll_language, present in the default list), meaning the plugin's cookie-cache feature must be enabled with at least one tracked cookie name configured.

context: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, LinkController::update() in app/Http/Controllers/API/LinkController.php passes $request->all() to the repository update method even though user_id is fillable and is not an allowed field in the validated update request. An authenticated API user who is authorized to update a link can therefore assign an arbitrary or nonexistent user_id, transferring the link into another user's bookmark collection or orphaning it from any real account. The web update controller is unaffected because it passes only validated fields. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

context: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the HTML bookmark import action in app/Actions/ImportHtmlBookmarks.php uses the global Link::whereUrl() lookup instead of restricting duplicate detection to the importing user. An authenticated user can submit a chosen URL and distinguish the skipped response count from the queued count to learn whether any account has saved that URL, including as a PRIVATE bookmark. The oracle reveals URL existence but does not directly return the bookmark contents or owner. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

context: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. Unlike the web list controller, which invokes LinkListPolicy::view(), the feed controller lets a normal authenticated user enumerate another user's private list or tag and receive its name and feed metadata, along with public or internal bookmark entries associated with that taxonomy. The existing per-link visibility filter still excludes PRIVATE link records, so the disclosure is limited to the private taxonomy and its non-private member links. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

context: The Shortcodes Ultimate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in versions up to, and including, 7.9.1 This is due to su_get_current_url() interpolating the raw Host request header into the authority portion of a URL that is then passed to esc_url() — which by design preserves '[' and ']' inside the authority so IPv6 literal hosts remain valid — and the [su_qrcode] shortcode substituting that value into its data attribute (the documented %CURRENT_URL% token) before feeding it to do_shortcode(). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include arbitrary PHP files that reside within the active theme's root directory (bounded because '/' inside an attribute value terminates parse_url()'s host and is then percent-encoded and stripped), and — when the shipped-default 'Unsafe features' option remains on — to read arbitrary post meta of any post, on any front-end page that renders [su_qrcode data="%CURRENT_URL%"].

context: The Unbounce Landing Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.6. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on the proxy error message that is persisted to the 'ub-proxy-error-message' option: unauthenticated attacker-controlled REQUEST_URI data is concatenated into the error string in UBHTTP::stream_request_curl()/stream_request_wp_remote() and stored via update_option(), then later echoed inside a <textarea> on the Unbounce Pages Diagnostics admin page without any escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user (an administrator viewing the Diagnostics screen) accesses an injected page.

context: The One to one user Chat by WPGuppy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'userId' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.6 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The plugin's permission callback is trivially bypassed because it validates a JWT that the plugin itself signs using an attacker-supplied value from the guppy_guest_account cookie, and the guest code path (userType=0) skips the get_userdata() check that would confirm the userId corresponds to a real WordPress user.

context: On Windows, the tarfile "tar" and "data" extraction filters did not reject member names or link targets that have a drive but no root, such as "C:foo". When extracting to a relative destination, such a member was written to the current working directory of that drive instead of the destination, and a symbolic link with such a target pointed outside the destination. The filters now refuse these member names and link targets with AbsolutePathError and AbsoluteLinkError.

context: The FV Player 8 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data.videos[].fv_wp_flowplayer_field_splash' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. context: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.2, sl_createCNIDArray in etc/afpd/spotlight.c assumes every element of kMDQueryItemArray points to an eight-byte uint64_t and copies sizeof(uint64_t) bytes from the indexed p->dd_talloc_array element without validating the element's talloc type or allocation size. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can use FPSpotlightRPC to supply a mixed-type sl_array_t containing a shorter boolean, nil, or string element, and an unauthenticated client can reach the same path when the optional guest UAM and a guest-accessible volume are enabled. The resulting eight-byte read extends beyond the shorter element's heap allocation and supplies an internal CNID filter; no confidentiality channel, write primitive, or code execution was demonstrated, while a production crash would require additional heap placement conditions. The container-type validation added for CVE-2023-42464 does not validate each element inside an accepted sl_array_t and therefore does not resolve this issue. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

context: Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.2, the Spotlight RPC consumer handlers sl_rpc_fetchAttributeNamesForOIDArray, sl_rpc_storeAttributesForOIDArray, and sl_rpc_fetchAttributesForOIDArray in etc/afpd/spotlight.c dereference the first element of a decoded sl_cnids_t without checking whether the inner CNID array is empty. An authenticated AFP client, or a guest when guest AFP access is enabled, can send a crafted SPOTLIGHT_CMD_RPC whose outer CNIDS length is greater than 16 while its inner count is zero, causing sl_unpack_cnids to create an empty DALLOC_CTX and the consumer to dereference dd_talloc_array[0]. The affected afpd child crashes, normally limiting denial of service to the attacker's session, and no memory write or code execution was demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.2.

context: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, the Cypher parser accepted an unbounded number of projection items in RETURN and WITH clauses while projection executors indexed fixed 32-element stack arrays using the parsed count. A query_graph query with more than 32 projection items could therefore write beyond those arrays, and a related result-column path could read uninitialized stack slots even when no node matched. Any caller of query_graph, including an agent whose query is influenced by untrusted content, could cause a reliable server crash and potentially compromise process confidentiality and integrity. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

context: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. context: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.10.0, the indexer's .gitignore matcher implemented * and ** through recursive backtracking without a work bound. context: In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the `cipher.AEAD` returned by `SecretKey.NewGCM()` passes whatever nonce it is given straight to `CK_GCM_PARAMS` without checking its length against `NonceSize()`, and accepts an empty nonce. On a token that accepts a zero-length GCM IV — SoftHSM2 does — every `Seal` with an empty nonce encrypts under the same IV, reusing the keystream and exposing the GHASH authentication key, which allows forgeries. Separately, `Config.UseGCMIVFromHSM` sends a NULL IV with length zero to the token unless `GCMIVFromHSMControl.SupplyIvForHSMGCMEncrypt` is also set, so the token has nowhere to write the IV it generates: a `Seal` with a non-empty nonce panics after the plaintext has already been encrypted, and a `Seal` with an empty nonce returns ciphertext under an empty IV without error. On the v1 line HSM-IV mode additionally never copies the token-generated IV back to the caller, so the caller keeps its own nonce while the data was encrypted under another one.

context: The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '_tutor_profile_bio' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. context: RabbitMQ is a messaging and streaming broker. In the affected revision identified by the advisory, the AMQP 1.0 server_mode parser in deps/amqp10_common/src/amqp10_binary_parser.erl stops at the first body section and preserves the remaining bytes in bare_and_footer without validating message-section order. An authenticated publisher with write permission can place a properties section carrying a forged user-id after the body, causing rabbit_access_control:check_user_id/2 to see no user-id while permissive downstream AMQP 1.0 decoders or AMQP 0-9-1 conversion through classic and quorum queues expose the forged identity. Applications that rely on RabbitMQ-validated user-id metadata can therefore accept attacker-controlled publisher attribution. Strict consumers that reject out-of-order sections are not vulnerable to identity spoofing, and the issue does not bypass broker routing or destination authorization. This issue is fixed in version 4.3.5.

context: Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, a BASIC application user, or an unauthenticated visitor to a public write form, can store markup in a shared external datasource that a builder or administrator later evaluates in any Handlebars binding Preview that surfaces the value, including the Data-section Formula column editor or any binding drawer. jsonFormatter.format() in packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts leaves raw strings and object keys unescaped, while packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte inserts the formatted result as raw HTML. The Handlebars SafeString path preserves the attacker-controlled value, and the Builder origin lacks a Content-Security-Policy that would block the resulting script. This permits stored script execution in the higher-privileged builder or administrator session rather than the writer's own role, allowing privileged Builder API actions and workspace data access. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

context: Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, the public POST /api/global/users/init endpoint on a self-hosted single-tenant deployment accepts an attacker-controlled tenantId and evaluates checkAnyUserExists() in the selected tenant database instead of the legitimate default tenant. An unauthenticated attacker can select an unused tenant namespace to bypass the one-time initialization guard, causing packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts to create a tenant-specific CouchDB database and a global-administrator document without a session or CSRF token. Repeating this operation with unique tenant identifiers can exhaust datastore resources and leave latent privileged records. The created administrator cannot log into the default tenant while multi-tenancy remains disabled, which limits the immediate impact to persistent writes, denial of service, and records that may become usable during later multi-tenant operation or migration. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

context:
Spring Data Elasticsearch replaces positional placeholders in string-based @Query methods with the method arguments before it evaluates SpEL expressions in the resulting query string.



As a result, an argument that contains a SpEL expression is evaluated as part of the query, even if the declared query does not use SpEL.



 An application is affected if it passes untrusted input as an argument to a repository query method that declares a @Query with positional placeholders.



In that case, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary code in the application, and repeated requests can exhaust memory through the unbounded expression cache.

context: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.5 through 4.0.9, the plugin matches path-scoped Express middleware with a matcher that requires a non-empty value for a dynamic segment, while Fastify's router accepts an empty parameter or wildcard value. When a route and an Express middleware mount share a dynamic pattern, a request with an empty segment matches the Fastify route and runs the handler while the middleware mounted on that pattern is skipped, so on a scoped mount an unauthenticated request can reach a protected handler. No special configuration is required, and the practical impact depends on what the empty value selects in the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

context: The Nexter Blocks Pro plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.10 via the `tpgb_ajax_register_user()` function. This is due to a byte-level denylist on the `tpgb_acf_key[]` and `tpgb_acf[]` parameters that fails to block Unicode look-alike characters — such as U+1E87 and U+00E7 in a key like `ẇp_çapabilities` — whose UTF-8 byte sequences do not match any ASCII-based pattern check, while the database's default accent-insensitive collation (`utf8mb4_unicode_ci` / `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`) treats the decorated key as equivalent to the canonical `wp_capabilities` row, causing `update_user_meta()` to overwrite the newly registered user's role with `administrator`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to register a new account bearing the full Administrator role, gaining complete control over the WordPress site including the ability to install plugins, modify files, and execute arbitrary code. The nonce required by the handler is publicly emitted on any page containing the tp-login-register block, making the full exploit chain — nonce retrieval, a single crafted registration POST, and the plugin's own `autologin` flow — trivially reachable on any default install where user registration is enabled. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

context:
Cleartext storage in encrypted parquet file vulnerability in Apache Arrow Rust (`parquet` crate), from version 55.0.0 through to 57.3.2, 58.4.1, 59.3.2 and 60.1.0.



When writing an encrypted parquet file with a column with bloom filters, the header and bitsets of the bloom filter are written in plaintext in the final parquet.



Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 57.3.3, 58.4.2, 59.3.3 or 60.2.0 which fix the issue by raising an error when trying to write encrypted parquet files with bloom filters enabled, preventing such files from being written out.



Existing encrypted parquet files written with bloom filters are still vulnerable, and it is recommended to rewrite those files with bloom filters disabled if possible.

context:
Improper Input Validation vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix (Phoenix.Presence) allows an attacker who can join a channel to cause a denial of service via a non-string presence key.

track/3,4 accepts any term as the presence key, such as a JSON object taken from a join payload. The key is converted with to_string/1 only later, in Phoenix.Presence.group/1, which raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a map. group/1 runs whenever presences are listed and when each presence diff is broadcast, together with the application's fetch/2, which can likewise raise on an unexpected key. Once such a key is tracked, every process that lists presences on the topic crashes, typically each channel that joins it, and presence diffs for the topic are lost.

From 1.7.0 the diff runs in a Task.Supervisor.async task linked to the tracker shard, and Phoenix.Presence.handle_info/2 has no clause for its failure. The shard then terminates, taking down every channel and LiveView process tracked on it and erasing presence state for all its topics. Repeated joins exhaust the restart intensity and take down the application supervisor.

This issue affects phoenix: from 1.2.0 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

context:
Improper certificate validation vulnerability in Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) libdigidocpp, Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc4, Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc on Android, and Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc on iOS.


The vulnerability occurs because libdigidocpp does not properly validate
 the Extended Key Usage (EKU) extension of certificates used to sign 
OCSP responses. Specifically, it fails to verify that the certificate 
contains the id-kp-OCSPSigning EKU, which identifies certificates 
authorised to sign OCSP responses. 





This issue affects libdigidocpp: from 3.10.0 before 4.5.2; DigiDoc4: from 4.0.0 before 4.11.2; DigiDoc: from 3.0.0 before 3.2.0; DigiDoc: from 3.0.1 before 3.2.0.

context: The Social Media Auto Poster – Schedule & Publish to Buffer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.9. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to delete Buffer sync log history for and disclose Buffer sync log contents of arbitrary posts, including those authored by administrators. The nonce used as the sole gate is not bound to any specific post ID, so a nonce harvested from the attacker's own draft editor screen is valid against any arbitrary post ID submitted in the request.

context: The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. context:
Uncaught Exception vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service via a client-selected legacy serializer on binary channel broadcasts.

When an application broadcasts {:binary, data} payloads on a channel topic, any client that connects without a vsn parameter, or with vsn=1.0.0, and joins that topic makes those broadcasts fail. Phoenix.Channel.Server.send/4 encodes each broadcast with every subscriber's own serializer inside the PubSub dispatch loop, calling fastlane!/1 with no rescue, and the negotiated Phoenix.Socket.V1.JSONSerializer raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a binary payload. Every binary broadcast on the topic then crashes the broadcasting process and skips every subscriber dispatched after the attacker. For broadcasts arriving from other nodes the loop runs in the PubSub adapter worker, whose repeated crashes restart the PubSub supervisor and empty the node's subscription registry while sockets stay connected.

This issue affects phoenix: from 1.5.7 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

context: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, the plugin joins a path-scoped middleware's mount path to the Fastify plugin prefix by string concatenation, so when the plugin prefix ends with a slash or the mount path omits its leading slash, the resulting Express mount path does not line up with the route the Fastify router serves. Express then fails to match and passes the request on while the Fastify router still dispatches the route, so the middleware is silently skipped. An application that uses path-scoped Express middleware for authentication or authorization inside a prefixed plugin can expose protected routes to unauthenticated clients, with no crafted request and no non-default option required, and string, array, and regular-expression mount paths are all affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

context: When the last EoE fragment has the TIME_APPEND flag set, the handler subtracts 4 from rxframeoffset to strip the timestamp. There is no check that rxframeoffset is at least 4. context: FOE_read and FOE_write store the filename length as uint8_t, truncating it modulo 256. When (mbxheader.length - ESC_FOEHSIZE) is a multiple of 256, the length becomes 0. Additionally, a request whose mailbox length equals ESC_FOEHSIZE exactly also produces a length of 0 without any truncation. In both cases FOE_fopen calls strncmp with a length of 0, which always returns equal, so the first registered file whose password is 0 is opened regardless of the filename the master sent.

context: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, when Fastify routing is configured to be case-insensitive, the router folds the request path to lower case in a way that maps certain non-ASCII Unicode characters to ASCII letters, but @fastify/express matches Express mount paths against the decoded path without applying the same folding. The two disagree, so a request that spells a letter of a mount path with an equivalent Unicode character is routed to the protected handler while the path-scoped middleware mounted on that path never matches and is skipped. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, though only when the application enables case-insensitive routing and the mount path contains an affected letter. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

context: mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.

context: MaxKB is an open-source AI assistant for enterprise. Prior to 2.10.7-lts, custom Tool Init Param definitions accept attacker-controlled props_info.rules[].validator strings through POST /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool and PUT /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool/{tool_id}, store them without restriction, and pass them to eval() when the parameter form renders. An authenticated user with the default USER workspace role can store JavaScript and trigger execution by opening the tool's Debug screen before entering or submitting a parameter value. The same Init Param form is exposed to accounts with edit permission on the tool, but execution by a different account was not independently verified. The confirmed script runs in the MaxKB origin; access to another user's bearer token and authenticated account authority is plausible only if that user renders the malicious form. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.7-lts.

context: The Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (initial store via wp-comments-post.php) / CSV cell on import' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. context: svglib reads SVG files and converts them to other formats. Prior to 2.3.1, the svg2rlg() renderer recursively expands nested SVG <use> references by deep-copying each referenced subtree; SvgRenderer.renderUse() in src/svglib/svglib.py calls xlink_href_target(), which rejects direct cycles but permits acyclic reference graphs with repeated fan-out. A small attacker-controlled SVG can therefore trigger exponentially increasing node expansion, consuming excessive CPU and memory in any application that renders it without a non-default option; HTML-to-PDF workflows using xhtml2pdf can reach the same renderer when an embedded data:image/svg+xml image in an HTML img element is passed to pisa.CreatePDF(). This issue is fixed in 2.3.1.

context: wcmatch is a Python library for wildcard file-name matching. Prior to 11.2, under the default flags, matching a non-matching attacker-controlled name against an application-supplied pattern containing several star wildcards separated by literals makes the lazy .? and [^/]? segments, including _STAR and _PATH_STAR emitted by _handle_star() in wcmatch/_wcparse.py, backtrack across possible splits, so a single comparison can consume prolonged CPU time. The pattern remains a developer-controlled constant and only the name is attacker-controlled; affected paths include fnmatch.fnmatch(), glob.globmatch(), and filesystem glob scans where another user can create names, without enabling extglob or any non-default flag. This issue is fixed in 11.2.

context: Inscriptis is a Python library for converting HTML to text. From 2.0.0 until 2.7.6, when the parent is block-level, table_end_handler() in model/tag/table_tag.py writes each sibling table through HtmlElement.write_verbatim_text() in model/html_element.py; Canvas.open_block() leaves the parent padding_inline prefix on the stack, Canvas.close_block() does not remove it, and only Canvas.close_tag() calls prefix.remove_last_prefix(). Each following sibling table therefore carries forward accumulated indentation, making get_text() output grow quadratically and allowing small attacker-controlled HTML to exhaust memory in applications converting it without authentication or user interaction. This issue is fixed in 2.7.6.

context:
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use TLS 1.3 early data using the ssl_early_data on directive, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS 1.3 connection to drive an NGINX worker into a tight loop in which it repeatedly retries the same send without ever making progress. The worker continues accepting new connections and handling existing ones, but one CPU core is pinned at 100%.

Impact:
System performance can degrade until the NGINX worker process is either forced to restart or is manually restarted. This vulnerability may allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a degradation of service that can lead to a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.

Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

context: @fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.10, the plugin passes Express a request URL that does not always match the path Fastify's router dispatched, so path-scoped Express middleware can be skipped while the route handler still runs. Several request forms trigger the mismatch, including percent-decoding that rewrites a backslash to a slash or double-decodes an encoded percent sign, and a request target that begins with an asterisk, so the middleware and the handler disagree on the path or on parameter and query values. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, with no special configuration required. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

context: @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards an incoming HTTP request to an upstream server. In versions before 12.9.1, when the plugin forwards a request whose body is not written to the upstream connection, such as a GET, HEAD, or TRACE request that carried a body, or a request with a falsy JSON body, it still forwards the client's Content-Length header while sending no body. The upstream server then treats the bytes of the following request as the unfinished body, which an attacker can use to desynchronize the connection and smuggle a request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.9.1, and users should upgrade to 12.9.1 or later.
